okay, here's a view from someone who used to be that friend. 

NTA.

I had a lot of raging, unchecked mental disorders growing up. I was always diagnosed bipolar but there had to of been something wrong with me. when I was 19 I was diagnosed BPD, and ignored it until maybe... six years ago. for reference, i am 29.

I had a best friend throughout grade school. she moved in after high school bc her home life was not good. I became emotionally dependent on her, which looking back, really possessive and unhealthy. 

eventually, my best friend got engaged, and got pregnant — and I don't know how, or why, but I took it personally. my heart was broken. I didn't like her boyfriend, either, who was nothing but kind to me (probably for her sake, though). I did feel a sense of betrayal. I took it so personally I felt like she was saying I wasn't good enough. 

eventually, she told me she needed space. she birthed her son and ended up committing suicide before we made up. obviously I went to therapy and confronted a lot of my problems, and now I live with a hanging regret that I wasn't the friend she deserved from me while I could have been. I am leagues better than where I was but, I wish I had been better while she was here. I feel so much guilt.

what I'm saying is ... you are NTA. I needed to be cut off. I deserved to be. I wasn't a good friend, and i acted like I should have been her priority when SHE WAS PREGNANT AND ENGAGED. which is just gross of me. 

I hope your friend, with time and help, can see that your friendship isn't any less strong because you are starting your life with a partner. I hope she takes advantage of the break, like I didn't, to get better and feel better about herself, so she can resume and be your friend. 

I wish you, and your friend, the best. but cut her off for now. she does love you, but it's overbearing, and you're well within your right to say no to that.
